note: Shows blocks with a chart per step: each block adds one note, and its own neck puts exactly the notes named so far in play (enable) and rings the one just added (highlight), ending on a tune made of only those notes. The neck shows the frets and the note names, so the text names only the degrees; the key and tempo are moves, so the text names no selector and its line about another key opens with {{?key}}.

exercise.title: Do, Mi, Sol on the neck, one note at a time
exercise.why: Do, Mi and Sol are the three notes of the home chord, so adding them one at a time shows how a tune is built from a chord you can already fret.

cells.text:
The neck below shows the {{=key}} major scale near the open strings, with only {{1}} in play. Find it on the A string, then on the B string, and hop between the two.
Practice until your hand finds each {{1}} without you looking at the neck.

{{3}} joins it, ringed on the neck below. From each {{1}}, find the nearest {{3}} above it. Play the pair, then play it backwards.
Practice until you find the {{3}} above any {{1}} without searching for it.

{{5}} joins them, ringed on the neck below. Start on the lowest {{1}} and play {{1}}, {{3}}, {{5}}, then back down through {{3}} to {{1}}.
Practice until you can play it without looking at the neck.

Press Play below to hear a short tune made of only these three notes, and play along with the neck.
Practice until you can hum the tune before you play it.
{{?key}}In another key the three notes sit on other frets, and the tune keeps its shape: up from {{1}} through {{3}} to {{5}} and home.
